blocks.etymology: From Middle English unclenchen, equivalent to un- + clench.

examples: The baby stopped crying and unclenched her fists.
wiktionary.gloss: To open (something that was clenched).

examples: Bill, take some deep breaths and unclench.
wiktionary.gloss: To relax, especially one's muscles.

blocks.etymology: From un- + constraint.

thesaurus.definition: the trait of lacking restraint or control; reckless freedom from inhibition or worry

vi_block: Trạng thái không bị ép buộc, trạng thái không bị gò bó.

wiktionary.gloss: Freedom from constraint.

blocks.etymology: From un- + intelligence.

wiktionary.gloss: Lack of intelligence.

blocks.etymology: From ward + -ship. Cognate with Dutch waardschap, Central Franconian Wirtschaff, Hunsrik Wertschaft, German Wirtschaft.

wiktionary.gloss: The state of being a ward of someone.
In English feudal law, the guardianship which the lord had of the land of his vassal while the latter was an infant or minor.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English waik, wayk, wayke, weik, weyk, borrowed from Old Norse veikr (“weak”), from Proto-Germanic *waikwaz (“weak, yielded, pliant, bendsome”), from *wīkwaną (“to cease, fold, yield; to retreat”), from Proto-Indo-European *weyg- (“to bend, turn, wind”), from *weh₁y- (“to plait, twist, weave, wind; to cover, enclose, wrap”). Cognates

senses.definition: Having little physical power or energy, especially because of illness, tiredness, or old age.

examples.en: She was still too weak to get out of bed.
examples.vi: Cô ấy vẫn còn quá yếu để rời khỏi giường.

examples.en: My legs felt weak after the long run.
examples.vi: Chân tôi bủn rủn sau chuyến chạy dài.

senses.definition: Not firm or solid enough to carry weight, support pressure, or resist being damaged.

examples.en: Do not climb that tree because it has weak branches.
examples.vi: Đừng trèo lên cái cây đó vì cành của nó rất yếu.

senses.definition: Not believable or persuasive because it lacks good evidence or strong reasons.

examples.en: He offered a weak excuse for missing the meeting.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đưa ra một lời bào chữa thiếu sức thuyết phục cho việc vắng mặt ở cuộc họp.

senses.definition: Not skilled at doing something or performing poorly in a particular subject.

examples.en: I was always weak at chemistry in school.
examples.vi: Tôi luôn học kém môn hóa học ở trường.

senses.definition: Containing too much water and lacking a strong taste or effect.

examples.en: This tea is far too weak for my taste.
examples.vi: Trà này quá nhạt so với khẩu vị của tôi.

senses.definition: Lacking willpower or courage, and easily controlled or influenced by other people.

examples.en: He was too weak to resist the temptation.
examples.vi: Anh ta quá yếu đuối nên không cưỡng lại được sự cám dỗ.

senses.vi: yếu đuối; mềm yếu; nhu nhược

senses.definition: Not bright, loud, or intense, and therefore difficult to notice.

examples.en: A weak light guided us through the dark tunnel.
examples.vi: Một ánh sáng le lói dẫn lối chúng tôi qua đường hầm tối tăm.

examples.en: The radio signal became very weak in the mountains.
examples.vi: Tín hiệu radio trở nên rất yếu ở vùng núi.

senses.vi: yếu ớt; le lói; mờ nhạt

senses.definition: Losing value or experiencing very low activity in trade or commerce.

examples.en: A weak currency makes imported products more expensive.
examples.vi: Một đồng tiền mất giá làm cho hàng nhập khẩu trở nên đắt đỏ hơn.

thesaurus.definition: overly diluted; thin and insipid
(used of vowels or syllables) pronounced with little or no stress
wanting in moral strength, courage, or will; having the attributes of man as opposed to e.g. divine beings
lacking bodily or muscular strength or vitality
deficient in magnitude; barely perceptible; lacking clarity or brightness or loudness etc

vi_block: Thiếu nghị lực, yếu đuối, mềm yếu, nhu nhược.

examples: The child was too weak to move the boulder.
They easily guessed his weak computer password.
wiktionary.gloss: Lacking in force (usually strength) or ability.

examples: a weak timber; a weak rope
wiktionary.gloss: Unable to sustain a great weight, pressure, or strain.
Limp, soft.

examples: weak resolutions; weak virtue
wiktionary.gloss: Unable to withstand temptation, urgency, persuasion, etc.; easily impressed, moved, or overcome; accessible; vulnerable.
Having a strong, irrepressible emotional love for someone or (less often) something; sentimentally affected by such love.

examples: We were served stale bread and weak tea.
wiktionary.gloss: Dilute, lacking in taste or potency.

examples: The verb to walk is weak because it has a past tense of walked and all forms are inflected by adding the typical suffix (ie is regular) to the stem walk- (ie has no vowel changes).
The verb to run is strong, not weak, because the past tense is ran.
wiktionary.gloss: Regular in inflection, lacking vowel changes and having a past tense marked by /-d-/, /-t-/, or /-ð-/.
Showing less distinct grammatical endings.
Definite in meaning, often used with a definite article or similar word.

examples: In some Semitic languages such as Akkadian, some or all gutturals are weak and often disappear, but in others such as Arabic and Ugaritic, they are strong and never disappear.
The reflexes of the Proto-Semitic verb *mawut- (“to die”) are often weak due to the presence of w, for example: Arabic مَاتَ (māta), Hebrew מֵת (mēṯ), and Ugaritic 𐎎𐎚 (mt /⁠māta⁠/).
wiktionary.gloss: Related to, containing, or being a consonant which is prone to disappearing in some inflections, in most applicable languages including (but not limited to) w and y.

examples: The Finnish verb kääntää (“to translate”) inflects to the singular imperative as käännä, showing the weak gradation nt > nn because it historically ended in a consonant which closed the syllable.
wiktionary.gloss: Related to, being, or containing the lenis consonant gradation, which resulted from historically closed syllables.

Of a form in which the accent tends to shift forwards (to the right, in transcription) or did so ancestrally in Proto-Indo-European, relative to the strong stem (which has the leftmost accent allowed).
In a grammatical case other than nominative, accusative, vocative or sometimes locative singular.
In a conjugation other than singular active forms (regardless of person, tense etc.).
Lenis, pronounced with less force or less markedness.

examples: a weak acid
a weak base
wiktionary.gloss: That does not ionize completely into anions and cations in a solution.
One of the four fundamental forces associated with nuclear decay.

examples: This place is weak.
wiktionary.gloss: Bad or uncool.
Having a narrow range of logical consequences; narrowly applicable. (Often contrasted with a strong statement which implies it.)
Resulting from, or indicating, lack of judgment, discernment, or firmness; unwise; hence, foolish.

examples: The prosecution advanced a weak case.
wiktionary.gloss: Not having power to convince; not supported by force of reason or truth; unsustained.

examples: a weak sentence; a weak style
wiktionary.gloss: Lacking in vigour or expression.
Not prevalent or effective, or not felt to be prevalent; not potent; feeble.

examples: a weak market; wheat is weak at present
wiktionary.gloss: Tending towards lower prices.

examples: a weak negative
wiktionary.gloss: Lacking contrast.

idioms.gloss: To fail to accomplish an accomplishable task or to make an attempt at less than maximum effort; to "half-ass" or "fake the funk".
The weak cannot resist the decisions of the strong; power, not morality, decides the outcome of any dispute.
idioms.phrase: the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must

known: the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must

tatoeba.en: She always sides with the weak.
tatoeba.vi: Cô ta luôn đứng về bên yếu.

tatoeba.en: He thinks love is only for the weak.
tatoeba.vi: Anh ấy nghĩ rằng tình yêu chỉ dành cho kẻ yếu.

tatoeba.en: A person with weak eyes can't see far.
tatoeba.vi: Một người với mắt kém không thể nhìn được xa.

blocks.etymology: From the game of poker, in which chips laid down on the table are staked.

examples: He wasn't a very talented musician but, when the chips were down, he played well.
When the chips are down, you need to make tough decisions.
wiktionary.gloss: When the pressure is on; when the situation is urgent or critical.
